learningObjective: Reason about which parts of an MLP block can be fused into a single GPU kernel and where the fusion boundary lies for a Fused-QKV/-MLP style optimization.

canonicalClaims.claim: In modern LLM MLP blocks, the standard fusion boundary is 'up + activation' fused into one kernel with the down GEMM kept separate; the [B, N, F] intermediate is written to HBM once between them.
nonImplications: Does not imply full-block fusion is impossible, but it is uncommon in production libraries.
Does not imply that the intermediate write to HBM is free — it is a real cost, just less than the alternative fusion penalties.

misconceptions.claim: up + activation + down can be trivially fused into a single kernel by fusing along the F dimension.
misconceptions.whyWrong: down accumulates over F, so fusion would require restructuring down's tiling; standard MLP shapes rarely benefit.

misconceptions.claim: Any fusion of MLP components hurts due to register pressure.
misconceptions.whyWrong: up + elementwise activation is a well-known robust fusion win.

misconceptions.claim: up and down can be concatenated into a single wide GEMM.
misconceptions.whyWrong: up reduces over D and down reduces over F; different reduction axes cannot be merged.

implementationFacts: cuBLASLt and CUTLASS support elementwise epilogues on the up GEMM output.
For SwiGLU, the gate and up GEMMs can also be fused into one wide GEMM (sharing the input read), then silu*up elementwise, then down.
performanceScenarios: Memory-bound elementwise activation folded into the GEMM epilogue is essentially free.
The extra [B, N, F] HBM roundtrip for the intermediate is the main remaining cost.
